title: GUARD (fixed in e7bee11d9d) — was: a Unicode tag character (U+E0020-U+E007F) inserted on the line was drawn by zrefresh as a `<000e0067>` hex escape instead of a one-column printable glyph

spec.completer:
#compdef fzc0125

_sfz_main() {
  local -a _m _d
  _m=(  )
  _describe -1 'say "hi" now' _m
}
_sfz_main "$@"; _sfz_ret=$?
_sfz_w0='🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿'
compadd -U -Q -J _sfzwd -X 'width chars/cols' -- "emoji-flag=${#_sfz_w0}/${(m)#_sfz_w0}:$_sfz_w0"
return $_sfz_ret

observed.notes: Src/Zle/zle_refresh.c:1268-1272 draws a line character as a glyph only when `WC_ISPRINT(*t) && (width = WCWIDTH(*t)) > 0`; in a --enable-unicode9 build those are u9_iswprint / u9_wcwidth (Src/ztype.h:77, Src/zsh.h:3302), and wcwidth9 gives the tag characters one column, so zsh 5.9.2 paints the flag sequence as `🏴` plus six one-column cells and `${(m)#}` reports 8. Everything else falls to the `<%.08x>` escape at c:1358-1377.

observed_when_diverging.recorded_under: main at a9add374ed plus peer-lane uncommitted edits, target/debug/zshrs zshrs 0.13.56, against /opt/homebrew/bin/zsh 5.9.2, keys=tab

retired.why: zrefresh's main line loop and its status-line loop measured each character with the `unicode-width` crate, which calls a tag character zero-width, so it took the non-printable `<hex>` arm. Both loops now use ztype_h::WC_ISPRINT and zsh_h::WCWIDTH (u9_wcwidth), as the single-line refresh path already did.

controls.note: the same completer at the default TAB binding with a plain ASCII match agrees with or without the fix
